audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as continuation of the whirlwind: Job's first reply, renewed divine challenge, justice/pride questions, and Behemoth imagery. Behemoth is preserved as poetic/mythic wild creature language rather than flattened.

verses.restored: The Eternal answered Job and said:

familiar.text: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,

modern.text: And the LORD said to Job:

original.text: וַיַּ֖עַן יְהוָ֥ה אֶת אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: Shall one who argues with Shaddai correct him? Let the one who reproves the Divine answer it.

familiar.text: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

modern.text: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”

original.text: הֲ֭רֹב עִם שַׁדַּ֣י יִסּ֑וֹר מוֹכִ֖יחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה

verses.restored: Job answered the Eternal and said:

familiar.text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

modern.text: Then Job answered the LORD:

original.text: וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: Look, I am small. What shall I answer you? I place my hand over my mouth.

familiar.text: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

modern.text: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.

original.text: הֵ֣ן קַ֭לֹּתִי מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶ֑ךָּ יָ֝דִ֗י שַׂ֣מְתִּי לְמוֹ פִֽי

verses.restored: Once I have spoken, and I will not answer; twice, but I will add no more.

familiar.text: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

modern.text: I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.” The LORD Challenges Job Again

original.text: אַחַ֣ת דִּ֭בַּרְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה וּ֝שְׁתַּ֗יִם וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִֽיף

verses.restored: Then the Eternal answered Job from the whirlwind and said:

familiar.text: Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

modern.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

original.text: וַיַּֽעַן יְהוָ֣ה אֶת אִ֭יּוֹב מנ סערה וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: Gird your loins like a strong man; I will ask you, and you make it known to me.

familiar.text: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

modern.text: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.

original.text: אֱזָר נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי

verses.restored: Will you truly annul my justice? Will you condemn me so that you may be righteous?

familiar.text: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

modern.text: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?

original.text: הַ֭אַף תָּפֵ֣ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י תַּ֝רְשִׁיעֵ֗נִי לְמַ֣עַן תִּצְדָּֽק

verses.restored: Do you have an arm like the Divine, and can you thunder with a voice like his?

familiar.text: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

modern.text: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?

original.text: וְאִם זְר֖וֹעַ כָּאֵ֥ל לָ֑ךְ וּ֝בְק֗וֹל כָּמֹ֥הוּ תַרְעֵֽם

verses.restored: Adorn yourself now with majesty and height; clothe yourself with splendor and glory.

familiar.text: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

modern.text: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.

original.text: עֲדֵ֥ה נָ֣א גָֽא֣וֹן וָגֹ֑בַהּ וְה֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תִּלְבָּֽשׁ

verses.restored: Pour out the overflowings of your anger; look at every proud one and bring him low.

familiar.text: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.

modern.text: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.

original.text: הָ֭פֵץ עֶבְר֣וֹת אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּרְאֵ֥ה כָל גֵּ֝אֶ֗ה וְהַשְׁפִּילֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: Look at every proud one and humble him; tread down the wicked where they stand.

familiar.text: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

modern.text: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.

original.text: רְאֵ֣ה כָל גֵּ֭אֶה הַכְנִיעֵ֑הוּ וַהֲדֹ֖ךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם

verses.restored: Hide them in the dust together; bind their faces in the hidden place.

familiar.text: Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret.

modern.text: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.

original.text: טָמְנֵ֣ם בֶּעָפָ֣ר יָ֑חַד פְּ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם חֲבֹ֣שׁ בַּטָּמֽוּן

verses.restored: Then I myself will acknowledge you, that your own right hand can save you.

familiar.text: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

modern.text: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.

original.text: וְגַם אֲנִ֥י אוֹדֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי תוֹשִׁ֖עַ לְךָ֣ יְמִינֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Look now at Behemoth, which I made with you; he eats grass like an ox.

familiar.text: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

modern.text: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.

original.text: הִנֵּה נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ חָ֝צִ֗יר כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹאכֵֽל

verses.restored: Look, his strength is in his loins, and his power in the muscles of his belly.

familiar.text: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.

modern.text: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.

original.text: הִנֵּה נָ֣א כֹח֣וֹ בְמָתְנָ֑יו וְ֝אֹנ֗וֹ בִּשְׁרִירֵ֥י בִטְנֽוֹ

verses.restored: He bends his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are woven together.

familiar.text: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.

modern.text: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.

original.text: יַחְפֹּ֣ץ זְנָב֣וֹ כְמוֹ אָ֑רֶז גִּידֵ֖י פחדו יְשֹׂרָֽגוּ

verses.restored: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs like bars of iron.

familiar.text: His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.

modern.text: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.

original.text: עֲ֭צָמָיו אֲפִיקֵ֣י נְחוּשָׁ֑ה גְּ֝רָמָ֗יו כִּמְטִ֥יל בַּרְזֶֽל

verses.restored: He is the first of the ways of the Divine; only his Maker can bring near his sword.

familiar.text: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.

modern.text: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.

original.text: ה֭וּא רֵאשִׁ֣ית דַּרְכֵי אֵ֑ל הָ֝עֹשׂוֹ יַגֵּ֥שׁ חַרְבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: For the mountains bring him produce, and all the beasts of the field play there.

familiar.text: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

modern.text: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.

original.text: כִּֽי ב֭וּל הָרִ֣ים יִשְׂאוּ ל֑וֹ וְֽכָל חַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה יְשַֽׂחֲקוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Under lotus plants he lies, in the hiding place of reeds and marsh.

familiar.text: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

modern.text: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.

original.text: תַּֽחַת צֶאֱלִ֥ים יִשְׁכָּ֑ב בְּסֵ֖תֶר קָנֶ֣ה וּבִצָּֽה

verses.restored: Lotus plants cover him with shade; willows of the brook surround him.

familiar.text: The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

modern.text: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.

original.text: יְסֻכֻּ֣הוּ צֶאֱלִ֣ים צִֽלֲל֑וֹ יְ֝סֻבּ֗וּהוּ עַרְבֵי נָֽחַל

verses.restored: Look, if the river presses, he does not panic; he is confident though Jordan rushes to his mouth.

familiar.text: Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.

modern.text: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.

original.text: הֵ֤ן יַעֲשֹׁ֣ק נָ֭הָר לֹ֣א יַחְפּ֑וֹז יִבְטַ֓ח כִּֽי יָגִ֖יחַ יַרְדֵּ֣ן אֶל פִּֽיהוּ

verses.restored: Can anyone take him by his eyes, or pierce his nose with snares?

familiar.text: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.

modern.text: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?

original.text: בְּעֵינָ֥יו יִקָּחֶ֑נּוּ בְּ֝מֽוֹקְשִׁ֗ים יִנְקָב אָֽף
